claim: The note points the learner at 'the source', which a learner reviewing in Anki does not have.
evidence: Note: 'Suffix — attaches after a person's name; cannot be used after one's own name (written 〜さん (san) in the source)'.
fix: Drop the 'in the source' aside, or say what the 〜 means (something goes in front) without citing the book.

claim: The note points the learner at 'the source', which a learner reviewing in Anki does not have.
evidence: Note: 'Suffix — attaches to the end of a noun to mean 'is/am/are' (written 〜です (desu) in the source).'
fix: Drop the 'in the source' aside; the rest of the note already explains the placement.

claim: The note says お is used almost only for other people's things, but the hint's own example is みやげ 'souvenir', and the hint leans on two words no card teaches instead of おくに, which the learner meets in this unit.
evidence: Hint: 'the prefix on native words like なまえ (namae, "name") and みやげ (miyage, "souvenir")'. Note: 'It's used almost entirely for things belonging to the person you're talking to (or a third person), not your own things'. Neither なまえ nor みやげ is on any card in the ledger.
fix: Use おくに (taught on the okuni card) as the hint's example, and soften the 'almost entirely' claim or square it with the souvenir example.

claim: The English defines どちら by reference to どこ, a word no earlier card and no card in this chapter teaches.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Where (polite word for どこ)'. No card in the ledger or in chapter-1/chapter-1-extras has どこ.
fix: Gloss it without どこ, e.g. 'Where (polite)', and keep the note's おくにはどちらですか example.

claim: The card needs を, which the learner has never seen, and the note names it without saying what it does; the English 'Please (I'd like to see Tanaka-san)' also reads oddly as a prompt.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Please (I'd like to see Tanaka-san)'. Answer: 'たなかさんをおねがいします'. Note: 'Here おねがいします (onegaishimasu) follows a person's name + を (o) to ask a receptionist to call them over'. The extras card w2-harris-o-onegaishimasu explains を; this one does not.
fix: Use the English 'I'd like to see Tanaka-san, please.' with a reception-desk hint, and add one clause saying を marks the person you are asking for.

claim: The romaji splits ドイツじん as 'doitsu jin', while the deck's own ドイツじん card spells it 'doitsujin'.
evidence: Says: 'īe, doitsu jin desu'. Card doitsujin: 'Says: doitsujin'.
fix: Write 'īe, doitsujin desu' to match the vocabulary card.

claim: The target introduces someone else with こちらは but leaves さん off their name, which contradicts what every other card in this chapter teaches about naming another person.
evidence: Answer: 'こちらはイギリスのライアンです' ('This is Ryan from England'). Compare w2-kochira-hoffman note: 'さん (san) stays on because you are naming somebody else', and san-suffix-ch14: 'cannot be used after one's own name'. ks3-tanaka-nozomi, fib-c1-this-is-brown and w2-kochira-harris all keep さん after こちらは.
fix: Either add さん (こちらはイギリスのライアンさんです) or add a note explaining when さん is dropped when introducing someone; also gloss イギリス as 'the United Kingdom' to match the igirisu card.

claim: The note claims a name without さん 'can only mean' yourself, but another card in this unit uses a bare name for someone else.
evidence: Note: 'Compare ハリスです (Harisu desu), which can only mean 'I am Harris'.' Card irl-l1-28: 'こちらはイギリスのライアンです' = 'This is Ryan from England'.
fix: Soften to 'normally means' once irl-l1-28 is settled, or fix irl-l1-28 so the rule holds.

claim: The note says every other の in the lesson joins a company to a person, which the learner can see is false from other cards in this unit.
evidence: Note: 'Every other の (no) in this lesson joins a company to a person; here it is plain possession.' Compare w2-raja-no-okuni-q 'ラジャさんのおくに', w2-watashi-no-kuni-nihon 'わたしのくに', and irl-l1-28 'イギリスのライアン'.
fix: Say instead that here の marks possession, as opposed to the company-and-person の of the introductions.

claim: The English drops the -san that the target has, unlike every other sentence card in the chapter, so a learner following the English could leave さん out.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Is Jack French?'. Answer: 'ジャックさんはフランスじんですか？'. Compare ex2b-smith-british-q 'Is Smith-san British?'.
fix: Write 'Is Jack-san French?'.

claim: The romaji splits フランスじん as 'furansu jin', while every nationality card taught in the base unit runs じん on (amerikajin, igirisujin).
evidence: Says: 'Jakku san wa furansu jin desu ka?'. Card amerikajin: 'Says: amerikajin'.
fix: Write 'furansujin' to match the other nationality cards.

claim: The English drops the -san the target has and says 'English' where the deck taught イギリスじん as 'British'.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Is Ryan English?'. Answer: 'ライアンさんはイギリスじんですか？'. Card igirisujin: 'British (person)'; ex2b-smith-british-q: 'Is Smith-san British?'.
fix: Write 'Is Ryan-san British?'.

claim: The romaji splits イギリスじん as 'igirisu jin', while the deck's igirisujin card spells it as one word.
evidence: Says: 'Raian san wa igirisu jin desu ka?'. Card igirisujin: 'Says: igirisujin'.
fix: Write 'igirisujin'.

claim: The romaji splits フランスじん as 'furansu jin', unlike every nationality card in the base unit.
evidence: Says: 'furansu jin'. Card amerikajin: 'Says: amerikajin'; doitsujin: 'Says: doitsujin'.
fix: Write 'furansujin'.

claim: The romaji splits かんこくじん as 'kankoku jin', unlike every nationality card in the base unit.
evidence: Says: 'kankoku jin'. Card chuugokujin: 'Says: chūgokujin'.
fix: Write 'kankokujin'.

claim: The romaji writes いいえ as 'iie' where every other card in the chapter writes 'īe'.
evidence: Says: 'iie, kokku desu'. Card iie: 'Says: īe'; ex2b-no-american: 'īe, amerikajin desu'.
fix: Write 'īe, kokku desu'.

claim: The note cites 'NOTES 2', a section of the book the learner reviewing in Anki does not have.
evidence: Note: 'NOTES 2 explains that そう (sou) stands in for the noun instead of repeating it'.
fix: State the point directly: 'そう (sou) stands in for the noun instead of repeating it'.

claim: The note cites 'the Key Sentence', book terminology the learner reviewing in Anki does not have.
evidence: Note: 'which is why the Key Sentence prints it in brackets: （わたしは）スミスです'.
fix: Refer to the card instead: 'which is why （わたしは）スミスです shows it in brackets'.

claim: ちがいます appears for the first time here and neither the answer nor the note says what the word itself means, so the learner memorises the phrase without knowing its parts.
evidence: Answer: 'No, that's not right.' Note: 'The negative counterpart of はい、そうです (hai, sou desu). Use it to deny the identification outright.' No card in the ledger has ちがいます.
fix: Add a clause to the note: ちがいます (chigaimasu) means 'that is different / that's wrong'.

claim: The note writes せんせい in kanji, which a learner who reads only kana cannot read.
evidence: Note: '(e.g. saying 先生 to or about them instead of their name)'.
fix: Write せんせい (sensei) in kana as the card does.

claim: The note explains the card by a scene ('Smith had already named it when asking for him') that the card never shows, so on its own it reads as a non sequitur.
evidence: Hint: 'introducing yourself with just your name'. Note: 'Tanaka drops the company here because Smith had already named it when asking for him.'
fix: Either put that situation in the hint, or make the note general: the company can be left out when the other person already said it.

claim: The category label on the Production front says 'School & Education' for a sentence about being an engineer; every other job card in the chapter is under 'Work & Occupations'.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'School & Education / I am an engineer.' Card irl-l1-36: 'Work & Occupations / Engineer'.
fix: Move it to 'Work & Occupations'.
